changes.text: 疫情头七周的结果，他整理成一张表。南华克和沃克斯霍尔公司供水40,046户，霍乱死亡1,263人；兰贝斯公司供水26,107户，死亡98人；伦敦其余地区256,423户，死亡1,422人。折算成每10,000户的死亡数，分别是315、37和59。不过，南华克和沃克斯霍尔公司的头七周数字并非全部逐户查得。在部分只由该公司供水的分区，怀廷医生的调查只做到8月5日，后三周的供水是按头四周的比例推算的；斯诺认为这一推算“必定非常接近真实”。他据此得出结论：南华克和沃克斯霍尔公司供水户的死亡率是兰贝斯公司供水户的八到九倍。但这只是疫情头七周的结果。斯诺自己说明，随着疫情推进，两组的悬殊“没那么大了”，不过仍然十分显著。疫情头四周是每万户71对5，相差十四倍；第二个七周是每万户537对115，接近五倍。截至10月14日的14周里，按每万居民计，南华克和沃克斯霍尔公司供水户死亡153人，兰贝斯公司供水户死亡26人。这组数字把795例供水不明的死亡平均分摊到其他各供水来源，两家公司供水户的人口也是登记总长的估计数。兰贝斯供水户的死亡率低于全伦敦，但并不低于北区和中区。

The first seven weeks of the epidemic went into a single table. Houses supplied by the Southwark and Vauxhall Company: 40,046, with 1,263 deaths from cholera. Lambeth Company: 26,107 houses, 98 deaths. The rest of London: 256,423 houses, 1,422 deaths. Per 10,000 houses that came to 315, 37 and 59. Not all of the Southwark and Vauxhall figures for the first seven weeks were checked house by house, though. In some sub-districts supplied only by that company, the inquiry of a medical man, Mr Whiting, extended only to 5 August, and the water supply of the last three weeks was calculated in the same proportion as in the first four weeks; Snow judged that this calculation "must be very near the truth". Snow's conclusion: "The mortality in the houses supplied by the Southwark and Vauxhall Company was therefore between eight and nine times as great as in the houses supplied by the Lambeth Company". That was the figure for the first seven weeks only. Snow himself wrote that as the epidemic advanced the disproportion "became not quite so great, although it continued very striking". In the first four weeks it had been 71 against 5 per 10,000 houses, fourteen times. In the second seven weeks it was 537 against 115 per 10,000 houses, nearly five times. Over the 14 weeks ending 14 October, there were 153 deaths per 10,000 living in houses supplied by Southwark and Vauxhall and 26 in houses supplied by Lambeth. These figures distribute the 795 deaths whose water supply was not ascertained equally over the other sources of supply, and the population of the houses supplied by the two companies is the Registrar General's estimate. The Lambeth figure was lower than London at large, but not lower than the north and central districts.

必须说清楚：本篇所有数字与叙述都出自斯诺本人的书和表格。死者住址来自登记总署。8月26日以后，各区登记员应登记总长的要求，填报了霍乱死亡病例发病房屋的供水情况。这些填报并不完整，仍有一批个案的供水没有查明。斯诺写道，这些填报与他对疫情早期的调查结果“完全一致”。这算是来自登记数据的部分印证，不过我们也只是通过斯诺的书才知道这一点。另外，调查并非全部出自斯诺之手：伯蒙德西等一些只由南华克和沃克斯霍尔公司供水的地区，是由医生约翰·约瑟夫·怀廷（John Joseph Whiting）去调查的。怀廷的调查只覆盖疫情头四周（7月8日至8月5日），查的是死亡发生的房屋接的是公司的水、自家水井还是别的水源；在部分这类分区，后三周的供水是按头四周的比例推算的，并非逐户查得。即便如此，学说、统计和呈现它们的这本书都出自斯诺。这不意味着数据有错，但意味着我们读到的是一方的记录。

Plainly: every figure and every account in this piece comes from Snow's own book and his own tables. The addresses of the dead came from the General Register Office. After 26 August the district registrars, at the Registrar General's request, returned the water supply of the house of attack in cholera deaths. The returns were incomplete, and the supply "remained unascertained in a number of cases". Even so, Snow says they "agree entirely" with the results of his inquiry into the earlier part of the epidemic. That is partial corroboration from registration data, though it reaches us only through Snow's book. Nor was the whole inquiry Snow's own work. A medical man, John Joseph Whiting, made the inquiries in Bermondsey and certain other districts supplied only by the Southwark and Vauxhall Company. Whiting's part covered only the first four weeks of the epidemic, from 8 July to 5 August, and asked whether each house had the company's water, a pump-well or some other source; in some of these sub-districts the water supply of the last three weeks was calculated in the same proportion as in the first four weeks, not ascertained house by house. Still, the doctrine, the statistics and the book that presents them are all Snow's. That does not make the data wrong, but it does mean we are reading one side's record.

另一种做法（作者设想的替代方案，不是史实）：只比较各区的平均死亡率，或者拿富区和穷区对比。那样贫富、住房、职业都会混进来，水的作用就分不清了。斯诺实际走的是更费事的路：他亲自查了兰贝斯公司供水所及各区的每一例霍乱死亡，挨家查住址、查水，必要时装瓶回家化验；只由南华克和沃克斯霍尔公司供水的地区，则由怀廷医生调查，其中部分分区后三周的数字是按比例推算的。这样换来了两样东西。一是同一批混供街道里，按供水分开的死亡户数。二是按两家公司全部供水户计算的每万户死亡比较。

Another approach, and this is the author's counterfactual rather than history, would have been to compare average death rates by district, or rich districts against poor ones. Wealth, housing and occupation would then have crowded in, and the effect of the water would have been hard to separate out. What Snow actually did was more laborious. He inquired himself into every cholera death in the districts the Lambeth Company supplied: death addresses, house by house, and water carried home in phials. The districts supplied only by the Southwark and Vauxhall Company were covered by a medical man, Mr Whiting, and in some sub-districts the figures for the last three weeks were calculated in proportion. This yielded two things. One was counts of deaths by water supply for houses in the same intermixed streets. The other was a company-wide comparison per 10,000 houses.
最后，本篇用的是扫描本的OCR文本，书中不少数字在识别时已经错乱，例如兰贝斯迁址的年份被识别成“185S”，化验部分的数值也有乱码。因此本篇只用清楚可辨的数字，例如表九的户数、死亡数和每万户死亡数，以及肯宁顿的分户数字；迁址年份以斯诺脚注中的1852年为准；化验部分只写定性的差别。字迹清楚不等于逐户查得：表九中南华克和沃克斯霍尔公司的死亡数，有一部分是按比例推算的（见上文限定）。

Finally, this piece works from OCR text of a scanned copy, and many figures in the book came through garbled: the year of the Lambeth move reads "185S", and the numbers in the chemical test are corrupted too. Only clearly legible figures are used here, such as Table IX's house counts, deaths and deaths per 10,000 houses, and the Kennington figures; the year of the move follows Snow's footnote (1852); the chemical test is described only qualitatively. Legible is not the same as ascertained house by house: part of the Southwark and Vauxhall death count in Table IX was calculated in proportion (see the limits above).

全部数字与叙述出自约翰·斯诺《论霍乱的传播方式》1855年第二版（archive.org 的 OCR 文本）。8月26日以后，各区登记员应登记总长的要求填报了供水情况。这些数据并不完整，斯诺称其与他的结果一致。部分地区的调查由怀廷医生完成；他只调查了疫情头四周，部分分区后三周的供水是按比例推算的。14周的数字把795例供水不明的死亡平均分摊到其他供水来源，两家公司供水户的人口为估计数。这些情况都只能通过斯诺的书得知。“两组没有任何差别”是斯诺本人的断言，分组并非随机。OCR 有错乱，本篇只采用清楚可辨的数字，化验数值未引用。本篇不涉及后世评价与细菌学的后续发展。

Every figure and account comes from John Snow's On the Mode of Communication of Cholera, 2nd edition (1855), read through archive.org's OCR text. After 26 August, district registrars returned water-supply data at the Registrar General's request. The returns were incomplete, and Snow reports that they matched his results. Part of the inquiry was carried out by a medical man, John Joseph Whiting; he covered only the first four weeks of the epidemic, and in some sub-districts the water supply of the last three weeks was calculated in proportion. The 14-week figures distribute the 795 deaths whose water supply was not ascertained equally over the other sources of supply, and the population of the houses supplied by the two companies is an estimate. All of this is known only through Snow's book. "No difference whatever" between the two groups is Snow's own assertion, and the split was not random. The OCR is garbled in places: only clearly legible figures are used, and the chemical-test values are not cited. Later assessments and the development of bacteriology are not covered.
